Research themes

Three connected lines
of inquiry.

Research questions move from sound radiated by airfoils to the unsteady loads and performance of aerodynamic systems.

Aeroacoustics

Airfoil noise and sound radiation in turbulent flows.

Unsteady flows

Unsteady loading, tip-gap flow, and rotor–stator interaction.

Aerodynamic performance

Low-subsonic grid-fin performance and flight applications.

Conceptual research illustrations; not experimental images or simulation results.

Current work

Drone acoustic
localization.

An ongoing project exploring passive detection and localization from the sound of drone motors and propellers.

Research project

Listening for location.

The project aims to develop a passive system that detects and localizes drones from their acoustic signature.

  • Proposed methodsThe planned approach combines a microphone array, time- and direction-of-arrival estimation, and machine learning for sound classification and background-noise separation.
  • Current stageThe available project plan describes design and development planning, with offline signal-processing and machine-learning validation planned before real-time deployment and field evaluation.

Graduate research

Phuwanut Pataratawinun

Phuwanut Pataratawinun is pursuing an M.S. in Innovative Engineering for Sustainability (IES) at Chulalongkorn University. The graduate research work supports experiments, acoustic data collection, and signal processing.
